title: Hugging Face Transformers + FastAPI Microservice
description:
A self-hosted email classification service. Two Transformer models, fine-tuned from distilbert-base-multilingual-cased on your own labeled emails, predict urgency and department. A FastAPI app serves them with Redis caching; no external AI API is involved, so emails stay on your servers.

  • train.py fine-tunes both models from a CSV with a plain PyTorch loop and reports held-out accuracy and macro F1.
  • POST /classify returns labels, per-label scores and a needs_review flag when the confidence is low.
  • Identical emails are answered from the Redis cache; the service keeps working if Redis is down.
  • /metrics shows request counts, cache hits, latency and the label distribution; Docker Compose runs API and Redis.
implementationSteps: Export labeled support emails (subject, body, urgency, department) from your ticket system into a CSV.
Install the pinned dependencies (CPU build of PyTorch by default).
Run train.py: it fine-tunes distilbert-base-multilingual-cased once per task and prints held-out accuracy and macro F1.
Save the two models with their tokenizers to models/urgency and models/department.
Load both models in the FastAPI app at startup and clean each email (quotes, signature, whitespace) before tokenizing.
Return labels, scores and a needs_review flag when the lower of the two confidences is below MIN_CONFIDENCE.
Cache results in Redis by a SHA-256 hash of the email for one hour, and ignore cache errors.
Expose /health and /metrics, and start API and Redis with docker compose up.
Retrain regularly with agent corrections and compare the new held-out metrics before you replace the models.
performance:
Targets, not measured results:

  • Classification accuracy of 85 % or more on a held-out split of your own emails before you enable automatic routing; train.py prints the actual value.
  • Expected well under 200 ms per email on a modern CPU (two DistilBERT passes, up to 256 tokens); repeated emails are served from the cache. Measure on your hardware.
  • Scale by running more API containers; the models are read-only.
userExperience: Developers call one JSON endpoint from the ticket system or a mail hook and get urgency, department and confidence back. Interactive API docs are available at /docs. Support teams see tickets pre-sorted, and low-confidence ones are marked for manual review. Data never leaves your infrastructure.
